about.title: About Trust Calculator - Estate Planning and Trust Analysis Tool
about.description: The Trust Calculator is a comprehensive estate planning tool designed to help you analyze trust fund distributions, calculate beneficiary payments, and evaluate trust performance over time. This calculator analyzes trust assets, distribution rates, growth assumptions, and time periods to project trust values and beneficiary income. Whether you're setting up a trust or managing existing trust assets, this tool provides accurate trust financial projections.

faq.q: How much should a trust distribute annually?
faq.a: Common distribution rates range from 3-5% annually to preserve principal while providing income. Higher rates (5-7%) may be appropriate for shorter-term trusts. Consider the trust's purpose, beneficiary needs, and long-term sustainability.

Trust expenses include trustee fees (0.5-2% annually), investment management fees (0.25-1%), legal and accounting costs, tax preparation, and administrative expenses. These costs reduce the trust's net growth and available distributions.

faq.q: How do taxes affect trust distributions?
faq.a: Trust taxation is complex. Trusts may pay taxes on undistributed income, while beneficiaries typically pay taxes on distributions received. Income character (ordinary vs. capital gains) affects tax rates. Consult tax professionals for specific situations.

faq.q: Should trust distributions be fixed or variable?
faq.a: Fixed dollar amounts provide predictable income but may not keep pace with inflation. Percentage-based distributions maintain purchasing power but create variable income. Many trusts use hybrid approaches or include inflation adjustments.
